confirmedRules.smeQuestion: P0 panel doubts spec fidelity: Read legacy/debcred/sp_debcred_empresa.sp:1500-1732. The core Given/When/Then is largely correct: TRANSQUICK swaps @i_frm_pagcob for @i_frm_pagcob_spi when not null (1500-1502); TRANSBIMO sets @i_valor_tarifa=@i_valor_comision (1506-1508); when @i_valor_comision > 0, sp_grb_comision is called with the commission value and literal reference 'COBRO DE COMISION' (1512-1600); on @w_return!=0 or @@error!=0 or @w_cod_errord!=0 the code sets @w_sts_proc='X', does 'rollback tran' if @@trancount>0, writes sp_grb_mov_y_frmpgo with est_proceso 'X', valor_mov=@i_valor_comision and cod_error=@w_cod_errord, then returns (1606-1700). Two edge-case inaccuracies make the card not fully faithful as a parity contract: (1) The 122003 fallback is dead: @w_num_error is set to 122003 (1612) and overwritten by @w_cod_errord if non-zero (1614), but @w_num_error is never used afterwards; the movement record receives @w_cod_errord (1652) and the procedure returns @o_error = @w_cod_errord (1698-1700). So if sp_grb_comision fails via @w_return!=0 or @@error!=0 while @w_cod_errord stays 0, the legacy rolls back, records the failed movement with cod_error 0 and RETURNS 0 (not 122003). The card's 'Error 122003 generic, replaced by the returned code if non-zero ... the procedure returns that code' overstates the behavior. (2) The block at 1716-1730 (commit tran + return @w_cod_errord) is unreachable because any non-zero @w_cod_errord already triggered the return at 1700; the card does not claim a commit, which is fine, but the parameter text should note the fallback-code discrepancy. Fix: state that the returned/recorded error is @w_cod_errord as-is (may be 0 on a return-code-only failure) and that 122003 is computed but never emitted. P0 is justified: this step moves money (debits commission from the company account) and governs rollback of the entire debit, so a wrong result is financially costly and hard to reverse.

confirmedRules.name: Notification is routed to basic-account notifier or event engine by service classification
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Services flagged 'B' in the ad_notificacion_basica catalogue notify via pa_sat_pnotificacion with beneficiary data; all other services (defaulting to 'OTRO') raise a cob_internet event with debtor and creditor product codes.

confirmedRules.when: A successful debit reaches the notification step with a matching SMS service
confirmedRules.then: pa_sat_pnotificacion is invoked with the ordered value, the separate commission, beneficiary name and group reference from bp_detalle (falling back to history); for a service not in the catalogue the sp_eventos path is used instead
confirmedRules.parameters: Catalogue 'ad_notificacion_basica'; classification values 'B' and default 'OTRO'; event value = debit value, event cost = separate commission + second SWIFT value (lines 980-986)
edgeCases: A catalogue value other than 'B' or 'OTRO' sends no notification at all
Order detail lookups fall back to db_sat_his history tables when not found in live tables

confirmedRules.name: Event notification identifies debtor product and client, treating basic virtual accounts as savings
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: For the event-engine notification the debtor product is CTE for current, AHO for savings, and for virtual accounts VIR unless the account is a basic account (product 13) which is reported as AHO; the client id is read from the respective account master.

confirmedRules.then: @i_prod_deb = 'AHO' and @i_cliente = vi_cliente of that account

confirmedRules.name: Stray result set and debit-value override for TRANSCLI/TARJCRED/COMEXT
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: The code emits an unnamed result set of commission and ordered value before overriding the debit value; this appears to be leftover debugging output.

confirmedRules.when: The notification step for TRANSCLI runs
confirmedRules.then: A two-column result set (@i_comision, @i_valor_ordenado) is returned to the caller in addition to the normal outputs
confirmedRules.parameters: Services: TRANSCLI, TARJCRED, COMEXT
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: Line 882 'select @i_comision, @i_valor_ordenado' is a bare SELECT that returns a result set to the caller; likely debug leftover that may break callers that read result sets.

confirmedRules.name: Generic notification is suppressed by the SAT block list or for BCE payroll without a debit account
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: The generic event notification is not raised when an active entry in 'ba_bloqueaNotificacionSAT' matches 'service-smsService' and the calling procedure name, nor when the channel is BCE, the service is ROLPAGO and no debit account is present.
confirmedRules.given: A ROLPAGO debit with SMS service 'ROL' invoked from procedure 'sp_x', and an active block-list entry named 'ROLPAGO-ROL' with other-field 'sp_x'
confirmedRules.when: The generic notification step evaluates the block list
confirmedRules.then: The event is not created; the debit is still recorded as successful

edgeCases: Block-list match is per calling procedure, so the same service may notify from one caller and not from another
BCE exception can never trigger via the normalised channel values (DIR/SAT/BNK/VEN) — only when the raw channel is literally 'BCE'
Debit account null with tipcta 3/4/12 would already have failed the debit, so the BCE exception is practically limited to ledger-account (type 9) flows — SME to confirm
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: Is the BCE/ROLPAGO/no-account exception still reachable in production, and is the block list intended to be keyed by the calling procedure name?

confirmedRules.name: Notification cost equals separate commission plus the second SWIFT value
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: The cost reported in the customer notification is the commission attributable to the order plus the second SWIFT commission, and the notified amount is the debit value.
confirmedRules.given: A TRANSWIFT order with separate commission 12.00 and second SWIFT value 5.00, debit value 1,000.00
confirmedRules.then: Notified value = 1000.00 and notified cost = 17.00
confirmedRules.parameters: cost = isnull(w_valor_comision,0) + isnull(i_valor2_swift,0); for TRANSWIFT w_valor_comision = i_valor_comision, for TRANSCLI/TARJCRED/COMEXT it is i_comision, otherwise null (0)
edgeCases: For services outside TRANSWIFT/TRANSCLI/TARJCRED/COMEXT the commission component is 0 and only valor2_swift contributes
Values are converted to varchar(11): amounts of 100,000,000.00 or more would be truncated

confirmedRules.name: Order data is read from the live payments database first and from the SAT history database when the order has already been archived
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Whenever the procedure needs order header or detail data (originating service of an SPI return, beneficiary/institution for notifications, order-header state update), it looks in the live db_biz_pagos tables and, if no row is found, repeats the lookup or update against the db_sat_his history tables.
confirmedRules.given: An SPI return (affectation 12) for order 5001 which has been moved to bp_orden_his
confirmedRules.then: or_servicio is taken from db_sat_his..bp_orden_his and the movement is attributed to that service

confirmedRules.name: Debit payment form defaults to the order payment form, and TRANSQUICK commissions use the SPI payment form when supplied
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: If no specific debit payment form is given, the order's payment form is used to select which header rows move to Transition; for TRANSQUICK, when an SPI payment form is supplied, it replaces the payment form used to resolve the separate-commission accounting configuration.
confirmedRules.given: A TRANSQUICK order with payment form 'CUE' and SPI payment form 'COB', and no explicit debit payment form
confirmedRules.when: The main debit finishes and the commission step starts
confirmedRules.then: The header update (option 01) targets rows with te_frm_pagcob = 'CUE'; the commission transaction/causal is looked up with payment form 'COB'
confirmedRules.parameters: i_frm_pagcob_deb = isnull(i_frm_pagcob_deb, i_frm_pagcob) at line 262; override only when service = 'TRANSQUICK' and i_frm_pagcob_spi is not null
edgeCases: Override happens after the main movement was recorded, so the main movement keeps the original payment form while the commission uses the SPI one
Other services ignore i_frm_pagcob_spi entirely
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: Is it intended that only TRANSQUICK uses the SPI payment form for the commission configuration, while the main debit record keeps the original payment form?

confirmedRules.name: Order header state update falls back to the historical order table and treats a null state as Initial
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: When moving an order header from Initial to In-Transition, a row whose process state is null is treated as Initial, and if no matching row exists in the live order table the same transition is attempted on the historical (SAT) order table before deciding that nothing was updated.
confirmedRules.given: Order 5001 whose header row has already been archived to db_sat_his..bp_total_orden_his with te_estado_proceso null
confirmedRules.when: The debit succeeds and the header transition runs
confirmedRules.then: The live update affects 0 rows, the historical row is updated to state 'T' with the debit error code, and the 'no header updated' error 122004 is not raised
confirmedRules.parameters: Initial state = 'I' (null coerced to 'I'); target state = 'T'; live table = bp_total_orden; fallback table = db_sat_his..bp_total_orden_his
edgeCases: A header already in state 'T' or any non-Initial state is not updated (idempotence guard) and, if nothing else matches, triggers error 122004 unless the service is exempted
The same live-then-history fallback is used to find the originating service of an SPI refund (lines 1352-1370)
Channel list for the option-based branch includes DIR, SFR, FR2, BTH and VEN; other channels use the collection payment-form set COB/TRC/CTB/CPD/TPD

confirmedRules.name: A failed debit note is committed as a recorded failure and returned as an output error code, not as a procedure error
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: If the debit note itself failed, the order's movement is still persisted with status X and the error code, the transaction is committed, and the debit-note error code is returned to the caller in the output parameter, bypassing the general error handler (so no rollback and no COBIS error message even when invoked from COBIS).
confirmedRules.given: A debit on account type 5 (not allowed) producing debit error 122001
confirmedRules.when: The movement with status 'X' has been recorded successfully
confirmedRules.then: The transaction is committed, @o_error = 122001 and the procedure returns 122001 without calling the COBIS error routine; if instead recording the movement fails, error 122002 goes through the rollback path
confirmedRules.parameters: success status = 'P'; failure status = 'X'; account-type error = 122001; movement-recording error = 122002
edgeCases: Return value equals the error code on this path, whereas the normal error path returns 0 when @i_aplcobis = 'N' — callers must handle both conventions
Comment at line 1314 says allowed types are 3, 4 or 9 while the code at 414 allows 3, 4 and 12
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: Inconsistent return convention: this path returns the error code as the procedure's return value while the lbl_error path returns 0 with @o_error set when not invoked from COBIS.

confirmedRules.name: Virtual-account debit is flagged as batch unless invoked from COBIS online
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: The debit is marked as a batch operation for the virtual-accounts debit note whenever the caller is not the COBIS online application (aplcobis = 'N'), and as online when aplcobis = 'S'.
confirmedRules.given: A debit to a virtual account (account type 12) invoked with aplcobis = 'N'
confirmedRules.when: The automatic virtual debit note (sp_vi_ndc_automatica) is called at line 654
confirmedRules.then: The batch flag passed is 1; with aplcobis = 'S' the flag is 0
confirmedRules.parameters: aplcobis 'S' -> batch 0; aplcobis 'N' (default) -> batch 1
edgeCases: If aplcobis is any value other than 'S' or 'N', the batch flag stays NULL and is passed as NULL to the virtual debit note
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: Does the virtual-accounts debit note behave differently (e.g. limits, notifications, cut-off) when the batch flag is 1 versus 0, and is NULL for an unexpected aplcobis value an acceptable outcome? | Does the virtual-account engine behave differently for batch=1 versus batch=0 (e.g. skips online limits or holds), and should a modernized service keep the SAT channel constant regardless of the original order channel?

confirmedRules.name: Payroll (ROLPAGO) payment start date is no longer stamped on the order
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: An earlier rule that set the order's payment start date (or_fch_inicio_pagcob) to the process date for ROLPAGO orders after a successful debit has been disabled (commented out, ref20) because virtual accounts are not in SAT; the procedure now commits without stamping it.
confirmedRules.given: A ROLPAGO order successfully debited on process date 2026-09-27
confirmedRules.when: The debit completes and the transaction is committed
confirmedRules.then: bp_orden.or_fch_inicio_pagcob is NOT updated by this procedure
confirmedRules.parameters: Service = 'ROLPAGO'; former error code 122005 on update failure (no longer raised)
edgeCases: Any consumer that relied on this start date being set here must obtain it elsewhere
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: Is the payment start date for ROLPAGO orders now set by another process, or is the field simply unused? Should the modernized service keep it disabled?
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: Dead code retained in the procedure; behaviour documented only by a comment

confirmedRules.name: SPI return (affectation 12) uses the company order number as the debit-note reference
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: When the service is SPI and the affectation type is '12' (SPI return/devolucion), the reference string sent with the debit note is replaced by the company order number, overriding whatever service-based reference was built earlier.
confirmedRules.given: An SPI order with @i_tipo_afec = '12' and @i_orden_empresa = 4587, for which the service-based reference was already built
confirmedRules.when: The debit note reference is finalized before posting
confirmedRules.then: @w_cadena becomes '4587' (the order company number as text); the earlier reference text is discarded
confirmedRules.parameters: Service literal 'SPI'; affectation type '12'; reference = convert(varchar(10), @i_orden_empresa)
edgeCases: Comparison uses ltrim/rtrim on service, so padded 'SPI ' matches
Older code (commented out, ref39) built the reference from catalogue ad_concepto_spi code '01'; it is no longer executed
Order numbers longer than 10 characters would be truncated by convert(varchar(10))
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: Block is effectively a no-op duplicate of the default assignment; safe to drop in a rewrite but confirm no downstream report depends on the concept description.

confirmedRules.name: Invocation context defaults: direct channel, affectation 10, batch flag derived from COBIS flag
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: When callers omit optional inputs, the debit is treated as a non-COBIS call (aplcobis 'N'), on the direct channel 'DIR', with affectation type '10' (standard debit), zero second SWIFT value and sequential 0; the COBIS flag also decides whether the virtual-account debit note is flagged as batch (batch = 1 only when aplcobis = 'N').
confirmedRules.given: A caller invokes the procedure without @i_canal, @i_tipo_afec or @i_aplcobis
confirmedRules.then: @i_canal = 'DIR', @i_tipo_afec = '10', @i_aplcobis = 'N', and @w_batch = 1 (passed to sp_vi_ndc_automatica for virtual accounts)
confirmedRules.parameters: Defaults: aplcobis 'N', canal 'DIR', tipo_afec '10', valor2_swift 0, secuencial 0; batch mapping S->0, N->1 at lines 176-178, used at line 654
edgeCases: Any @i_aplcobis value other than 'S' or 'N' leaves @w_batch null
@s_ssn defaults to 0 when null (line 266)
@i_frm_pagcob_deb defaults to @i_frm_pagcob when null (line 262)
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: Is the 'batch' flag for virtual-account debit notes intended to mean 'not invoked from COBIS online', and what does the virtual-account module do differently in batch mode?

confirmedRules.name: Cash/cheque/account tariff and commission breakdown is passed through to the separate-commission debit only
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: The six REF33 tariff/commission breakdown inputs (tarifa, comision_cue, tarifa_efe, comision_efe, tarifa_che, comision_che) are not validated or computed here; they are forwarded unchanged to the separate-commission debit note (lines 1590-1600), and the generic tariff is overwritten with the separate commission before that call (line 1508), while the second SWIFT debit uses the SWIFT value as its tariff (line 1820).
confirmedRules.given: A call supplying @i_valor_tarifa_efe = 1.50 and @i_valor_comision = 2.00
confirmedRules.when: The separate-commission debit note is posted
confirmedRules.then: The commission debit note receives valor_tarifa = 2.00 (overwritten from @i_valor_comision), valor_tarifa_efe = 1.50 and the other breakdown fields as supplied
confirmedRules.parameters: All six breakdown inputs default to null; main debit note does not receive them
edgeCases: @i_valor_tarifa supplied by the caller is silently replaced by @i_valor_comision at line 1508
Second SWIFT commission passes @i_valor2_swift as valor_tarifa
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: Are the cash/cheque/account tariff breakdown values meant to be informational for the commission movement only, or should they influence the amount debited?

confirmedRules.name: Virtual-account and ledger-account debits do not carry the bundled commission or card data
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Only current/savings account debits pass the bundled commission, transaction count, unit commission, card number and provider detail to the debit engine; virtual-account debits post the plain value with the causal and reference only.
confirmedRules.given: A debit of $100.00 with @i_comision = $2.50 (bundled), @w_cantidad = 5, @w_comision_und = $0.50
confirmedRules.when: The company account is virtual (type 12) vs current/savings (type 3/4)
confirmedRules.then: Type 3/4: sp_ndc_ahcc receives tcomision=$2.50, nchq=5, solca=$0.50, card, provider detail, SPI payment form and order refs. Type 12: sp_vi_ndc_automatica receives only value $100.00, causal, currency, company, reference; the bundled commission and counts are not posted.
confirmedRules.parameters: sp_ndc_ahcc: @i_frm_pagcob = @i_frm_pagcob_spi, @i_alterno_dos = @i_frm_pagcob, @i_secuencial = 0; sp_vi_ndc_automatica: no commission fields
edgeCases: Bundled commission normally moves to separate commission at lines 188-196, so @i_comision reaching sp_ndc_ahcc is usually 0 unless both were supplied > 0
Ledger accounts (type 9) go through sp_graba_tran_servicio with @i_indicador = 1 and @i_tipo_chequera = company id as text
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: Is it intended that virtual-account debits never bill the bundled commission or transaction count, or is that data simply not supported by the virtual engine?

confirmedRules.name: SWIFT notifications read the beneficiary institution and credit account from the order detail, falling back to history
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: For TRANSWIFT the notification data (beneficiary institution and credit account name, first 30 chars) is read from the live order detail matched by order, sequence and ordering company; if the order was already archived the SAT history tables are used; for all other services these fields are empty.

confirmedRules.when: Notification data is gathered after a successful debit
confirmedRules.then: @w_emp_inst = dt_referencia_grupo and @w_cta_cre = first 30 characters of dt_nom_cuenta from bp_orden_his/bp_detalle_his; notification commission = @i_valor_comision
confirmedRules.parameters: Match keys: or_orden_banco = @i_orden, dt_orden_banco, dt_secuencial = @i_secuencial (default 0), or_ordenante = @i_empresa; account name truncated to 30 chars
edgeCases: Non-TRANSWIFT services: institution and credit account set to NULL
If neither live nor history row matches, values remain NULL and notification proceeds anyway

confirmedRules.name: Second SWIFT commission failure aborts the whole debit; its 'record and return' branch is unreachable
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: If the second SWIFT commission debit fails, the entire transaction is rolled back and error 122003 (or the engine's own error) is raised; the code path that would commit and return the commission error as an output code can never run.
confirmedRules.given: A TRANSWIFT debit with @i_valor2_swift = $15.00 whose sp_grb_comision call returns @w_cod_errord = 122010
confirmedRules.then: Error 122010 is raised via lbl_error, the full transaction is rolled back and the main debit plus the first commission are reversed; the 'commit and return @o_error' branch at 1844-1854 is skipped because the goto fires first
confirmedRules.parameters: Default error 122003 'Error al generar debito por comision'; affectation '16'; tariff passed as @i_valor2_swift; beneficiary name = account name; @i_tipo_horario = @i_tipo_referencia
edgeCases: Unlike the main debit (which keeps a status-X movement), a second-commission failure leaves no recorded movement in this procedure (sp_grb_comision may record its own before the rollback discards it)
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: Lines 1844-1854 are dead code: the preceding check (line 1824) already jumps to lbl_error whenever @w_cod_errord != 0, so the intended 'reverse, record commission movement with error, return' behaviour documented in the comment at 1840-1842 does not occur.
